new_statements.translation: Although Olutyipungu is a tonal language, like most languages of the Bantu group, in this work we do not represent the tones. [p.15] ... apparently identical singular prefixes, namely omu- of classes 1 and 3, show distinct tonal properties (omù- (cl. 1) vs. omú- (cl. 3)) and trigger distinct agreement patterns [p.29]

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record for nyan1305 (no catalog record, no stress statement held by the project). The work adds only 'tonal language, tones not marked' for the Quipungo (Olutyipungu) variety, described as phonologically close to Olunyaneka; it neither places word stress nor denies it, so it cannot seed a stress-placement record. Compatible with the on-file note that the bibliography tag 'likely states stress' was optimistic: this thesis does not.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The author states only that Olutyipungu (which he treats as a variety conserving the phonetics/phonology of Olunyaneka, orthography after Lang 1906) is a tone language and that tones are left unmarked; one lexical/grammatical tone contrast is cited (cl.1 omù- vs cl.3 omú-). Nothing is said about word stress, accent, penultimate lengthening or prominence: a full-text search for stress/accent the full text for acento/acentua/stress/accent/tónic/penúltim/sílaba/proeminên/prosód/entoaç/alonga/duraç/intensidade returns no prosodic hit. The thesis has no phonology chapter (TOC: 1 Introdução, 2 Situação sociolinguística, 3 Estrutura morfológica, 4 Estruturas ditransitivas, 5 Considerações finais).
new_statements.identity_note: Nambalo 2021 describes Olutyipungu, the Quipungo (Tyipungu) variety of the Nyaneka-Nkhumbi cluster (title page R.13I, record R.12I), which the author places under Olunyaneka (Estermann 1960) or Olunkhumbi (Redinha 1974) and writes with Lang's (1906) Nyaneka orthography because it 'conserva muitos aspetos fonético-fonológicos do olunyaneka' (p.15); Olunyaneka proper [nyan1305] appears comparatively throughout ch.3 (72 mentions) but receives no prosodic description either.

sources.note: Bilingual Nyaneka-Portuguese folktales with an ethnographic/performance introduction; remarks on 'tonalidades e inflexões de voz' refer to storytelling delivery, not phonology. Silent on stress/tone.

sources.citation: Homburger, L[ilias]. 1925. Le groupe sud-ouest des langues bantoues. Mission Rohan-Chabot, Angola et Rhodesia (1912-1914), Tome III, fasc. 1: Linguistique. Paris: Imprimerie Nationale / Paul Geuthner. 209 views (~190 pp.).
sources.note: Comparative phonetics (ch. III, pp. 85-104) and morphology of 7 SW-Bantu varieties incl. Nyaneka (data from the Huíla mission grammars, no Nyaneka informant). Only mention of accent is a general remark on p. 85 (view 105): consonant correspondences 'n'étant pas généralement influencées par l'accent (bien qu'il y ait des faits propres à la finale)'. Nyaneka-specific remarks (pp. 97-98) concern aspiration of N+voiceless and loss of nasals before final i. No word-stress rule, no tone marking, no accent marks in the transcription key (pp. v-viii).
